reported.claim: The recursion checks only whether the whole text is empty, not whether text_index is past the end, so it indexes beyond the text and raises IndexError when a match reaches the end of the text.
reported.expected: [(0, 0, a), (0, 0, b), (2, 2, ), ...] i.e. a list of three tokens ending with a match, without error
reported.title: LZ77 _match_length_from_index raises IndexError past end of text

reported.claim: After emitting a run, the count is reset to 0 instead of 1, so every run after the first gets a count of 0 when the next character differs.
reported.title: run_length_encode resets count to 0 after a run

reported.claim: target_sum is set to 1, but the function is meant to find triplets summing to 0, so every valid triplet is missed.
reported.title: find_triplets_with_0_sum_hashing uses target sum 1 instead of 0

reported.claim: The inner loop starts at i = 1 instead of 0, so sparse_table[j][0] is never computed for j >= 1 and stays 0, giving wrong minimums for ranges starting at index 0.
reported.title: build_sparse_table inner loop starts at 1, leaving column 0 uncomputed

reported.claim: The loop compares values with `is not`, so an equal but non-identical int (e.g. any value outside the small-int cache) is never recognised as found, and the search walks off the tree and returns None.
reported.expected: The Node whose value is 1000, not None
reported.title: BinarySearchTree.search compares with 'is not' instead of !=

reported.claim: When a path sum matches the target the counter is decremented (-=) instead of incremented, so matching paths are subtracted from the count.
reported.title: BinaryTreePathSum decrements the count on a match

reported.claim: The guard is inverted (`if root:` instead of `if not root:`), so for any existing node the helper returns immediately and yields nothing.
reported.title: get_nodes_from_right_to_left populate_output guard inverted

reported.claim: The method only measures the path through its own node, so it misses longer paths that lie entirely inside a subtree.
reported.failing_call: Node(1, Node(2, Node(3, Node(4, Node(5))), Node(6, None, Node(7, None, Node(8))))).diameter()
reported.title: Node.diameter ignores paths entirely within subtrees

reported.claim: The early-return guard uses `head.next_node` where it should use `not head.next_node`, so any list with two or more nodes returns True without checking.
reported.title: is_palindrome_stack early-return guard wrong, returns True for lists of 2+ nodes

reported.claim: The outer loop starts at min(6, n - 1) instead of 1, so strip points with index below 6 are never compared with earlier points, missing the closest pair.
reported.title: dis_between_closest_in_strip loop starts at min(6, n-1) instead of 1

reported.claim: Elements equal to the pivot are dropped from both partitions, so with duplicates the recursion reaches an empty list and crashes in random_pivot.
reported.title: kth_number drops elements equal to the pivot, crashing on duplicates

reported.claim: When both inputs are square matrices, the function returns the two input matrices wrapped in a list instead of their product, so the multiplication is never performed.
reported.title: strassen returns the input matrices instead of their product for square inputs

reported.claim: The function returns dp[n][w_], where w_ is the leftover loop variable, instead of dp[n][w]; when w is 0 the inner loop never runs, so w_ is unbound and the call crashes.
reported.title: knapsack returns dp[n][w_] using a leftover loop variable

reported.claim: The first element is stored at tail[-1] (the last slot) instead of tail[0], so tail[0] is wrong and the length is overcounted.
reported.title: LIS O(n log n) stores first element at tail[-1] instead of tail[0]

reported.claim: The validation uses 'and' instead of 'or', so a zero or negative resistance is accepted as long as the other one is positive, even though the docstring says all values must be positive.
reported.expected: ValueError: All values must be positive
reported.title: astable_duty_cycle validation uses 'and' instead of 'or'

reported.claim: Reactive power should use sqrt(1 - pf**2), but the code uses sqrt(1 + pf**2), so the result is wrong for any nonzero power factor.
reported.title: reactive_power uses sqrt(1 + pf**2) instead of sqrt(1 - pf**2)

reported.claim: The loop upper bound `len(price_series) - 1` drops the last price, so the output is one element shorter than the input series.
reported.expected: A list of length 4: two leading nan values followed by two computed values (one per index from 2 to 3).
reported.title: fracdiff_fixedwindow loop bound drops the last price

reported.claim: randint(0, len(child)) - 1 yields indices -1 to len-1, so the last gene is chosen twice as often as others and index -1 aliases it; the intended range is randint(0, len(child) - 1).
reported.expected: Mutation position should be uniform over indices 0 to 5 (no index -1 wrap-around bias).
reported.title: mutate picks index with randint(0, len)-1, biasing toward the last gene

reported.claim: The longitude validation lost a `not` on the second clause, so any lon2 within [-180, 180] (the normal case) raises the ValueError.
reported.title: lamberts_ellipsoidal_distance longitude validation missing 'not', rejects valid lon2

reported.claim: The lower-hull orientation test uses lower_hull[-1] as the origin and lower_hull[-2] as the first point, which flips the sign of the cross product, so reflex turns are kept and non-hull points are returned.
reported.title: monotone_chain lower-hull orientation test has flipped sign

reported.claim: The vertical-line check compares v3.y with v2.y instead of v3.x with v2.x, so valid triangles with v1.x == v2.x and v3.y == v2.y are wrongly rejected as redundant.
reported.expected: A Triangle object is constructed without error
reported.title: Triangle.__post_init__ compares v3.y with v2.y instead of v3.x with v2.x

reported.claim: The degree-to-radian conversion is wrong: (angle % 360) / 450 * 180 / pi does not equal the angle in radians (it should be angle * pi / 180), so rotations use the wrong angle.
reported.expected: Rotation by pi/2, so the y and z components are rotated a quarter turn (about (1.0, -3.0, 2.0))
reported.title: rotate converts degrees to radians incorrectly

reported.claim: `set(start)` builds a set of the characters of the start name instead of containing the start node, so multi-character node names wrongly mark neighbours as visited and cut off paths.
reported.title: bfs_shortest_path_distance uses set(start), splitting multi-character node names

reported.claim: The recursive result of depth_first_search is discarded (`pass`), so a colour conflict found deeper in the traversal never propagates and odd cycles are reported as bipartite.
reported.title: is_bipartite_dfs discards the recursive result, missing odd cycles

reported.claim: The parent index is computed as floor(i/2), which gives the wrong parent for right children (e.g. index 2 maps to 1 instead of 0, index 4 maps to 2 instead of 1); it should be (i-1)//2.
reported.title: PriorityQueue.par computes the wrong parent index

reported.claim: The loop removes items from self.graph[u] while iterating over it, which skips the element after each removal, so consecutive matching edges are not all removed.
reported.failing_call: dg = DirectedGraph(); dg.add_pair(0, 5, 1); dg.add_pair(0, 5, 2); dg.remove_pair(0, 5); dg.graph[0]
reported.title: DirectedGraph.remove_pair removes items while iterating, skipping consecutive matches

reported.claim: When exactly two nodes have odd degree the function falls through (`pass`) and returns type 3 (not Eulerian) instead of type 2 (Euler path).
reported.title: check_circuit_or_path returns not-Eulerian for graphs with two odd-degree nodes

reported.claim: The function returns the count n instead of the donor-to-recipient matching list (donor_record), so the result never reflects the computed matching.
reported.title: stable_matching returns n instead of the matching

reported.claim: The visit Counter is seeded with each node at count 1 (Counter of the node list) instead of 0, so every node's visit count is inflated by one.
reported.title: get_transitions seeds visit counts at 1 instead of 0

reported.claim: The first cell of each row subtracts the cell above instead of adding it, so the cumulative path sums are wrong and the returned minimum can be too small.
reported.title: fill_row subtracts instead of adds the cell above

reported.claim: The remaining capacity subtracts weights[counter + 1] instead of the current item's weight weights[counter - 1], which gives the wrong capacity and raises IndexError when counter equals len(weights).
reported.title: knapsack_recur subtracts the wrong item's weight

reported.claim: The loop is a `for` over range(rank) fixed at the start, so it keeps visiting row indices that are already beyond the reduced rank, and the `row -= 1` on line 73 has no effect; a zero row past the current rank then decrements the rank again, giving a too-small result.
reported.title: rank_of_matrix loop over a fixed range mishandles reduced rank

reported.claim: The diagonal entries of the reflection matrix should be 2*c*c - 1 and 2*s*s - 1 (the standard reflection matrix), but the code uses 2*c - 1 and 2*s - 1.
reported.title: reflection matrix diagonal uses 2*c-1 instead of 2*c*c-1

reported.claim: prune builds the `pruned` list but returns `item_tuple`, a leftover loop variable, instead of the filtered candidates.
reported.title: prune returns a leftover loop variable instead of the pruned list

reported.claim: inc subtracts the occurrence count instead of adding it, so node counts decrease as transactions are inserted into the FP-tree.
reported.title: TreeNode.inc subtracts instead of adds the count

reported.claim: epsilon is subtracted inside the square root instead of added, so a zero moving average raises a math domain error rather than giving a finite step.
reported.title: rmsprop subtracts epsilon instead of adding it

reported.claim: The function returns side2 instead of the computed Heron's formula area, so the computed area variable is never used.
reported.title: area_triangle_three_sides returns side2 instead of the area

reported.claim: Taking abs of the sum fx2 + fx1 makes negative regions of the curve add positive area, so the result is not the signed area under the curve.
reported.title: trapezoidal_area takes abs of the sum, breaking signed area

reported.claim: After trial division, a leftover prime factor n > 1 is never multiplied into the sum, so its contribution (1 + n) is omitted, unlike the other factors.
reported.title: sum_of_divisors omits leftover prime factor

reported.claim: The origin latitude is read from origin[-1], which is the longitude, instead of origin[0].
reported.title: initial_bearing reads origin latitude from the longitude

reported.claim: The base case returns 0 for objects == 0, but the number of derangements of zero objects is 1 (D(0) = 1), which the recurrence seeds from.
reported.title: derangement base case for 0 objects returns 0 instead of 1

reported.claim: For a vertical line x = p1[0] the function returns C = p1[0], but with the Ax + By + C = 0 convention used by segment_intersection (a x + b y = -c), C must be -p1[0]; the sign is flipped, so intersections with vertical lines land at the mirrored x coordinate.
reported.title: line_coefficients returns wrong sign of C for vertical lines

reported.claim: The strict comparison x < b - h drops the last interior point b - h, so Simpson's rule omits one weighted term.
reported.title: make_points strict comparison drops the last interior point

reported.claim: The loop leaves prev_num holding P_n, but the function returns prev_prev_num, which holds P_(n-1), so every n >= 2 gives the wrong value.
reported.title: pell_number_iterative returns the previous value

reported.claim: The accumulator starts at 1 instead of 0, so the sum is inflated by 1 and the mean is wrong.
reported.title: arithmetic_mean accumulator starts at 1

reported.claim: The base case bell[-1] = 1 sets the last element (index max_set_length) instead of bell[0], so B_0 stays 0 and every later Bell number is wrong.
reported.title: bell_numbers sets bell[-1] instead of bell[0]

reported.claim: The loop runs only to number-1, so the result is the (number-1)th Catalan number instead of the nth; catalan(2) returns 1 and catalan(5) returns 14 instead of 42.
reported.title: catalan loop stops one short

reported.claim: The split range stops one short, so the split point equal to digits - 1 is never tried; for 9 (square 81, two digits) no split is tested and a valid Kaprekar number is rejected.
reported.title: is_kaprekar split range stops one short

reported.claim: The search starts at index 1, so the first row is never searched and a value present in row 0 is reported as missing.
reported.title: mat_bin_search skips the first row

reported.claim: The guard should check whether matrix_b is empty (`not matrix_b`), but it uses `matrix_b`, so any non-empty matrix_b returns an empty list.
reported.title: kronecker_product empty-matrix guard inverted

reported.claim: After each row, next_row is assigned the same list object as current_row, so the next row overwrites the values it still needs to read as the diagonal and bottom neighbours; it should be a copy.
reported.title: largest_square_area space-optimized version aliases rows

reported.claim: Scalar multiplication wraps each product in int(), so float scalars truncate results to integers instead of returning the scaled matrix, which breaks inverse() (it multiplies the adjugate by 1/det).
reported.title: Matrix.__mul__ truncates scalar products with int()

reported.claim: The multiply function calls _verify_matrix_sizes, which requires both operands to have identical shapes, so valid conformant products such as a 2x3 by 3x1 matrix are rejected.
reported.title: multiply requires identical shapes instead of conformant ones

reported.claim: The range stops one short (len - 1), so the last resource column is never summed and the returned list has one entry fewer than the claim vector.
reported.title: __processes_resource_summation skips the last resource column

reported.claim: tmp1 and tmp2 are the same dict object, so setting tmp2[p]=False overwrites tmp1[p]=True and the True branch is never explored with True.
reported.expected: (True, a model satisfying the formula, e.g. A1 True and A2 True)
reported.title: dpll_algorithm shares one dict between both branches

reported.claim: leap_day_reinstall_number uses true division (/ 4) instead of floor division, so the fractional value propagates and gives a wrong date for years such as 2100.
reported.title: gauss_easter uses true division instead of floor division

reported.claim: The loop range ends at len(sorted_points) - 1, so the last sorted point is never processed and can be missing from the hull.
reported.title: graham_scan skips the last sorted point

reported.claim: The capacity check is inverted: any nonzero n (including positive sizes) sets the capacity to sys.maxsize, while n == 0 sets it to 0, so the cache never evicts at the requested size and the n < 0 error branch is unreachable.
reported.title: LRUCache capacity check inverted

reported.claim: During the swap, previous_node.next is set to node.prev (the node before the swap pair) instead of the node's old next, and the neighbour links are never repaired, so the doubly linked list is corrupted and can form cycles.
reported.expected: 3, with the list kept consistent (no cycle)
reported.title: _position_node swap links wrong neighbours

reported.claim: The check uses `<= 0`, so a tangential force of exactly 0 raises an error, which makes the `tangential_force == 0` branch unreachable even though that case is meant to solve for the tangential force.
reported.title: shear_stress rejects zero tangential force

reported.claim: The feasibility test compares each deadline with the task's position in the reward-sorted list, including rejected tasks, instead of the number of tasks already accepted, so feasible tasks are dropped.
reported.title: max_tasks feasibility test uses sorted position instead of scheduled count

reported.claim: When a process arrives after the current time, the clock is advanced by adding its arrival time instead of setting it to the arrival time, so the clock overshoots.
reported.title: first_come_first_served advances clock by arrival time instead of setting it

reported.claim: When the current time is before a process's arrival, the clock is increased by the arrival time instead of being set to it, giving wrong completion times.
reported.expected: The finished deque's process has stop_time 8 (start at 5, burst 3)
reported.title: round_robin advances clock by arrival time instead of setting it

reported.claim: The full-group branch slices `arr[i:]` instead of the five-element window `arr[i:i+5]`, so the median is taken over the whole remaining list and the pivot is wrong.
reported.title: median_of_medians slices arr[i:] instead of a five-element window

reported.claim: The guard for n <= 1 is a bare pass instead of returning, so for an empty list block_size is 0 and range(0, 0, 0) raises ValueError instead of returning an empty list.
reported.title: kirkpatrick_reisch_sort does not return for empty input

reported.claim: The final insertion loop runs over range(len(sorted_list_2d) + 1), so on the last iteration it indexes sorted_list_2d[len], which is out of range; it should iterate over the groups only.
reported.title: merge_insertion_sort final loop goes out of range

reported.claim: The zeros bucket is recursed with bit_position + 1 instead of bit_position - 1, so the bit position never reaches 0 for groups of equal-bit numbers and the recursion never terminates.
reported.title: _msd_radix_sort recurses with bit_position + 1

reported.claim: The comparison checks collection[i - 1] < collection[i] but then swaps positions i and i + 1, so pairs are compared against the wrong neighbour and the list is not sorted.
reported.title: odd_even_transposition compares wrong neighbour

reported.claim: The validity test uses 'or' instead of 'and', so any 13-digit barcode is reported valid without checking its check digit.
reported.title: barcode is_valid uses 'or' instead of 'and'

reported.claim: The early-return check uses `m >= len(text)`, so a pattern exactly as long as the text is wrongly reported as not found even when it matches.
reported.title: bitap_string_match rejects pattern equal in length to text

reported.claim: The checksum is computed as `10 - subtotal % 10`, which yields 10 when the subtotal is a multiple of 10, so a valid PESEL with checksum digit 0 is rejected; it should be `(10 - subtotal % 10) % 10`.
reported.title: is_polish_national_id rejects checksum digit 0

reported.claim: The swap condition uses `<=` instead of `<`, so for two words of equal length it swaps and recurses forever, causing a RecursionError instead of returning the distance.
reported.title: levenshtein_distance_optimized recurses forever on equal-length words

reported.claim: For a word with no vowels the loop ends with i at the last index, so the last letter is moved to the front instead of the whole word being followed by 'ay'.
reported.title: pig_latin mishandles words with no vowels

reported.claim: The function returns the loop variable `word` (the last word of the sentence) instead of the `occurrence` dictionary it builds.
reported.title: word_occurrence returns last word instead of the dictionary
